### Signals Before Waking

Preparation may not be a last-second switch. In one study, seven successful participants showed right prefrontal changes about 30 minutes before waking. In a small nap study, heart rate began rising about three minutes beforehand. Different systems may join the transition on different timelines, rather than one signal predicting an exact alarm minute.

### Why It Can Feel Easy

Sleep changes across the night. Deep slow-wave sleep is more common earlier, while lighter NREM and REM sleep become more common later. Because waking from deep N3 sleep produces stronger sleep inertia than waking from N2, waking near the alarm may feel clearer simply because the brain is in a gentler stage—not because it has read the clock.

## In one line

The morning mystery may be less like a hidden alarm and more like several modest systems meeting at the right moment. That can feel uncanny without requiring perfect prediction.
